title: obw-championship
label: Sidster

won.source: James Parker's own page names him "then OBW Champion Sidster" being backed to a successful defense by the newly formed Flock (promotions/obw/archive/james-parker.html); the reign's own start is not otherwise dated in the surviving record.

how: Already champion when the Flock backed him to a successful defense at Rebirth (dated 2012-04-30 in this wing's own show ledger, obw-rebirth-2012) against a group of OBW Originals, welcoming James Parker into the stable in the process.
note: The surviving record does not say how or when this reign ended. Super Krmi is the next attested holder, but nothing establishes that Krmi followed Sidster directly rather than an unrecorded champion in between.

title: obw-championship
label: Super Krmi

lost.source: Chad Bowens's own page: he "would finally win the OBW Championship the next week by defeating Super Krmi" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html), naming Krmi as the champion he beat on the Storm episode after Storm's 54th; how or when Krmi won the title is not otherwise recorded.

how: Lost the title to Chad Bowens on the Storm episode following Storm's 54th.
note: Super Krmi's own caption calls him a multi-time OBW Champion; only this one reign is attested by name anywhere in the surviving record.

title: obw-championship
label: Chad Bowens

won.source: Chad Bowens's own page: "Chad Bowens would finally win the OBW Championship the next week by defeating Super Krmi" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html).

lost.source: The same page, immediately after: "This was short lived however as Ice cashed in his contract and defeated Bowens for the championship that night" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html).

how: Beat Super Krmi to win the title, then lost it that same night to a Money in the Bank-style contract cash-in by Ice.
note: Bowens's own bio credits him as a 2x OBW Champion; only this reign is attested by name anywhere in the surviving record, so a second reign cannot be reconstructed or dated.

title: obw-championship
label: Ice

won.source: Chad Bowens's own page: "Ice cashed in his contract and defeated Bowens for the championship that night" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html); Ice's own caption independently calls him "a one-time OBW Champion whose cash-in ended Chad Bowens's own reign."

how: Cashed in a contract to win the title from Chad Bowens the same night Bowens had won it.
note: Ice's own caption calls this his only OBW Championship reign. How or when he lost the title is not recorded — Chad Bowens was released from OBW that same fall, and the corpus does not narrate the men's title again until Punisher and Execution's own M-Star are already established rivals in early 2013.

title: obw-championship
label: Punisher

won.source: OBW's own champions list names Punisher as OBW Champion at its own last-touched revision of 21 February 2014 (promotions/obw/archive/obw-champions.html); Punisher's own caption independently calls him "the reigning OBW Champion as of the last-touched champions list." How or when Punisher won the title from Ice is not recorded — the corpus resumes the men's title story in early 2013 with Punisher already the Storm-side rival of Execution's own M-Star (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html).

how: Reigning champion at the wiki's own last-touched champions list; leader of the stable the Prophecy.
note: Still champion at the record's own last word; the record ends there rather than the reign, matching the convention already used for this wing's other still-open reigns.

title: obw-world-heavyweight
label: MVP Lux

lost.source: Chad Bowens's own page: "Prior to Bowens match with MVP Lux, Lux was attacked by Mr. Excellent, Ryan Daniels, Angelic Storm, and Darnell Jackson, thanks to these attacks Bowens was able to easily defeat MVP Lux to win his first OBW World Heavyweight Championship" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html), naming Lux as the champion Bowens dethroned; how or when Lux won the title is not otherwise recorded.

how: Lost the title to Chad Bowens on Execution, after being attacked by four other wrestlers just before the match.
note: Lux's own bio credits him only with four OBW Hardcore Championship reigns and does not mention this title at all, though it does record him winning an Elimination Chamber match at Death Trap (obw-death-trap-2012, 30 July 2012) for an open-ended championship opportunity "at anytime, any place" -- that show is not wired as this reign's own `event` since it records the opportunity being earned, not a title change.

title: obw-world-heavyweight
label: Chad Bowens

won.source: Chad Bowens's own page: "Bowens formed a new alliance named G3... Prior to Bowens match with MVP Lux, Lux was attacked... thanks to these attacks Bowens was able to easily defeat MVP Lux to win his first OBW World Heavyweight Championship" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html), dated by the same page to "June 25th, 2013 on Execution 86" -- no show by that name or date is in this wing's own show ledger, so the win is not wired to an `event`.

lost.source: The same page, immediately after: "tragedy struck Chad Bowens when an injury sidelined him and forced him to vacate the OBW World Heavyweight Championship" (promotions/obw/archive/chad-bowens.html).

how: Beat MVP Lux, with an assist from an outside beatdown of Lux by four other wrestlers, to win the title; vacated it after an in-storyline injury.
note: Bowens's own caption and bio both call him a one-time OBW World Heavyweight Champion, matching the single reign reconstructed here. How or when the vacancy was filled is not recorded.

title: obw-world-heavyweight
label: M-Star

won.source: OBW's own champions list names M-Star as OBW World Heavyweight Champion at its own last-touched revision of 21 February 2014 (promotions/obw/archive/obw-champions.html); M-Star's own caption independently calls him champion "as of the last-touched champions list." How or when M-Star won the title from the vacancy Chad Bowens left is not recorded anywhere in the surviving record.

how: Reigning champion at the wiki's own last-touched champions list.
note: Still champion at the record's own last word; the record ends there rather than the reign, matching the convention already used for this wing's other still-open reigns.
